_comment: The shelf, by what a thing IS rather than what it is about.
study_sources.json answers 'what am I doing this morning'. This answers
'where do I go to learn X' — it is a catalogue, not a schedule, and
nothing here is ever filed as a commitment or nags you.
Certification prices were checked on 2026-10-28 and every url is the
official page, so a rise is one click away rather than a rumour. They go
stale: re-check before paying. Prices are exam-only unless the note says
Add to any section by editing this file — title and url are the only

sections.label: Certifications
sections.blurb: Exam-only prices. The order inside each track is the order to take them.

groups.label: Solutions architect
groups.note: Cloud architecture, in the order of cheapest-first. AWS is the one most job ads name; the other two are worth holding only if you are targeting that cloud.

items.title: AWS Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03)
items.note: 130 min, 65 questions, valid 3 years. Take it first: cheapest by a factor of three and the most widely recognised.

items.title: AWS Solutions Architect – Professional (SAP-C03)
items.note: 180 min, 75 questions, valid 3 years. AWS recommends two or more years of designing and implementing on AWS before attempting it — it is a trade-off exam, not a facts exam.

items.title: Microsoft Azure Solutions Architect Expert (AZ-305)
items.note: The Expert badge needs AZ-104 (Administrator Associate) as well, so budget two exams. Price is per exam and varies by country.

items.title: Google Professional Cloud Architect
items.note: 2 hours, valid 2 years. Google recommends 3+ years industry experience, 1+ on GCP.

groups.label: Web3 security
groups.note: Read this before spending: in smart contract security a public audit record counts for more than any certificate. Contest placings on Code4rena, Sherlock or CodeHawks and a repo of findings are what firms actually read. The certificates below exist and are listed honestly, but treat them as structure for your own study, not as the credential.

items.title: Certified Smart Contract Auditor (Blockchain Council)
items.note: Exam-only has been listed around $299 and bundles around $349, so check all three pages before paying. Recognition in the audit industry is limited — it is a syllabus, not a door-opener.

items.title: CCSS Auditor (CCSSA) — CryptoCurrency Certification Consortium
items.note: Live virtual training, auditor track 2–4 days, one exam attempt included. This one is about auditing custody and key management against the CCSS standard, not about reading Solidity.

groups.label: Platform & offensive security
groups.note: The existing ladder. CKS cannot be attempted until CKA has been passed.

items.title: CKA — Certified Kubernetes Administrator
items.note: $645 with the LFS258 course. Valid 2 years, one retake and two Killer.sh attempts included.

items.title: CKS — Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist
items.note: $645 with LFS260. Requires a current CKA.

items.title: OSCP — Offensive Security Certified Professional
items.note: Course + exam bundle, or $2,749/yr for Learn One. Existing AWS holders have had up to 20% off Learn One — check before buying.

sections.label: Courses
sections.blurb: Worked through, not watched. Each one has exercises you can show afterwards.

groups.label: AWS Solutions Architect (SAA-C03)
groups.note: Everything here is free except where the price says otherwise. The exam is $150; the only thing worth paying for beyond it is a practice-question bank, because SAA is a question-reading exam as much as a knowledge one.

items.title: AWS Skill Builder — SAA-C03 exam prep plan
items.note: AWS's own four-step plan. Skill Builder has a free tier of 900+ courses; the full exam-prep suite including official practice exams is the $29/month subscription. AWS does not state which tier this plan sits in — check when you sign in.

items.title: SAA-C03 exam guide
items.note: The actual syllabus. Secure 30%, resilient 26%, high-performing 24%, cost-optimised 20% — study in proportion, not by interest.

items.title: AWS Well-Architected Framework
items.note: The vocabulary the exam and interviewers both use. Run a real review against something you own rather than reading it.

items.title: Disaster recovery of workloads on AWS
items.note: Backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby, multi-site. Scenario questions give an RTO and want the cheapest strategy that meets it.

items.title: AWS Architecture Center
items.note: Reference architectures. Read them as worked examples of the trade-offs the exam asks about.

items.title: AWS Pricing Calculator
items.note: Cost is 20% of the exam and the domain people leave until last. Price one of your own designs in it.

items.title: Exam booking — AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate
items.note: 130 min, 65 questions, valid 3 years. Check your AWS Certification account for a 50% voucher first — passing any AWS exam earns one for the next.

items.title: Cyfrin Updraft — Smart Contract Security
items.note: The most complete free security course. Do it with Foundry open.

items.title: Secureum — Smart Contract Security 101
items.note: The reading behind the RACE quizzes. Dense; treat each post as a session.

items.title: Damn Vulnerable DeFi
items.note: Solve by hand in Foundry before pointing any agent at it, or you cannot tell a missed bug from a bad prompt.

items.title: Ethernaut (OpenZeppelin)
items.note: Write why each level broke, not just the exploit.

items.title: OWASP Smart Contract Security
items.note: A checklist to audit your own code against.

items.title: RareSkills — Learn Solidity
items.note: The track that opens your day. One chapter, notes written as you go.

items.title: evm.codes
items.note: Opcode reference. Explain a gas cost aloud before moving on.

items.title: Solana Cookbook
items.note: Typed out, not copied.

items.title: Anchor — Solana framework docs
items.note: Explain a program's account constraints line by line.

items.title: The Move Book
items.note: Resources vs accounts, abilities, object ownership.

items.title: Alchemy University
items.note: RPC, indexing and infra, with exercises.

items.title: Hugging Face — LLM Course
items.note: Runs alongside the fellowship's first phase.

items.title: Hugging Face — Agents Course
items.note: Tool calling and agent loops, which is what the auditor is.

items.title: AI Engineering — Chip Huyen (O'Reilly)
items.note: One chapter a week, filed against the fellowship week.

sections.label: Articles & references
sections.blurb: Places to read from, not one-off links. Each is a well you go back to.

items.title: Solodit
items.note: Every public audit finding, searchable. Predict root cause and severity BEFORE reading the writeup.

items.title: yAudit reports
items.note: Short, well-argued reports — a good model for how to write your own.

items.title: Rekt
items.note: Exploit post-mortems. Read for the mechanism, ignore the theatre.

items.title: smart-contract-vulnerabilities
items.note: One entry a day, explained from memory afterwards.

items.title: yAudit — Common Web3 Security Issues
items.note: On the yBorg prep shelf.

items.title: samczsun
items.note: The standard for exploit writeups.

items.title: Paradigm research
items.note: Protocol design and MEV, written properly.

items.title: OpenZeppelin blog
items.note: Audit reports and proxy pattern explanations.

sections.label: Newsletters
sections.blurb: Inbox, once a week. If one stops being read for a month, drop it from this file.

items.title: Week in Ethereum News
items.note: The one that is worth the whole week's reading if you only keep one.

items.title: Secureum Substack
items.note: Security fundamentals and RACE quiz announcements.

items.title: Rekt
items.note: Also runs as a feed — same source as the post-mortems above.

items.title: The Batch (DeepLearning.AI)
items.note: Weekly, readable, not hype-led.

items.title: Import AI (Jack Clark)
items.note: Research-heavy. Good for fellowship paper leads.
